failure_patterns.pattern: endpoint_selection_and_call_set: Calls included redundant validators or unrequested providers, or selected an endpoint returning categories instead of matching products.

rejected_edits.content: - Build the smallest complete call set: cover every requested outcome, and make every call serve one of them. Treat explicitly named providers or platforms in a comparison as the requested source scope; do not add unnamed providers merely because the task asks for a comparison. Choose one endpoint for each distinct requested result property, and do not add another call when its result would repeat a property already covered. A request to use multiple tools means complementary checks for distinct requested properties, not every plausible validator. Use one endpoint for multiple outcomes only when it genuinely covers them; make separate calls for distinct inputs unless the schema supports batching. If an endpoint is unavailable, use a listed alternative only if it genuinely fulfills the request. Do not invent tools, add unrelated calls, or include redundant alternatives or validators.

rejected_edits.content: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields using accepted representations. For geographic and market fields, use the documented country, region, postal-code, or internal-ID form and canonical value; carry the location only to outcomes it qualifies. Do not substitute an arbitrary default market or guess an undocumented ID or code; if a required value cannot be derived from the request or documented schema, do not call that endpoint.

Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales.

rejected_edits.content: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap. Match the returned content type too: product discovery requires an endpoint that searches or suggests matching products; a category or taxonomy listing does not show whether matching products are carried.
